display.title: Episode 157: The Flickering Flame, Chapter 2 (Asarah B'Teves)
display.summary_short: A cobbler's words teach Rabbi Yisrael Salanter that 'as long as the lamp burns, one can still repair', and Uncle Yossi explains the fast of Asarah B'Teves and its promised future as a Yom Tov.
display.summary_long: Broadcast in the week of Asarah B'Teves. Uncle Yossi opens with the old riddle 'black and white and red all over' to introduce the new Tzivos Hashem newsletter, and after a march in which the whole family joins in, he reads from it about the Wonderful World of Shabbos exhibition. At Mitzvah Time a girl wins by listing ways to welcome Tati home from work, and a boy leads the Shema. The story concludes: the cobbler tells Rabbi Yisrael Salanter that he keeps working as long as his lamp is lit, because 'as long as the lamp burns, one can still repair.' Rabbi Yisrael hears a message from Heaven: the neshamah is Hashem's lamp, and as long as we are alive we can repair our mistakes through teshuvah, so we must never put off learning Torah and doing mitzvos. Uncle Yossi then explains Asarah B'Teves: the siege of Yerushalayim by Nevuchadnetzar that led to the breach of the walls on the Seventeenth of Tammuz and the destruction of the Beis HaMikdash on Tisha B'Av. We remember in order to improve ourselves, and Hashem has promised that with Moshiach these sad days will become days of joy.
display.lesson: As long as the lamp of life burns we can still repair through teshuvah; never put off a mitzvah until tomorrow.

date.note: 'This coming Thursday is the tenth day of Teves' (Thu 1985-01-03); Tuesday show. Exhibition 'January 6-7' still upcoming.

advisories.note: Explains the siege of Yerushalayim, hunger in the city and the destruction of the Beis HaMikdash.

privacy.note: Phone-in winner and Shema guest named in full.
